title: Adaptive partial-response / safety fallback sketch
content:
Quick scratchpad — thinking about a small feature set: adaptive partial responses + safety-aware fallbacks + budget-aware session routing. Mostly sketchy notes, user stories, and a rough rollout plan.

Problem statement
- Customers want predictable latency and cost but also to maintain safety and reasonable output quality. When model latency spikes (load, KV cache miss, long contexts) or a request exceeds configured cost/latency budgets, we currently either queue (high latency) or fail (bad UX).
- Need an approach that can: 1) gracefully degrade output instead of failing, 2) signal partial outputs to clients for progressive UX, and 3) route aggressively to lower-cost/safer alternatives under constraints.

Goals (MUST)
- Provide an API-level capability to return partial/streamed provisional responses when full generation would violate latency/cost SLOs.
- Have configurable fallback chains: e.g., full model -> quantized variant -> distilled/cheap model -> degenerate canned reply.
- Integrate safety checks so that cheap fallbacks do not bypass policy blocks; fallbacks must be safe-by-design or include filtering.

Non-goals (for MVP)
- No new training or model distillation pipelines. We will only wire existing model variants in the model catalog.
- Not building full client-side UI controls — just good server signals (headers, events) so frontends can decide how to show partial responses.

User stories
- As a product engineer, I want the API to return an early partial answer when the request would otherwise time out so my chat UI can show a preliminary response and then patch it when the final arrives.
- As an SRE, I want requests above latency percentile X to automatically route to cheaper model variants when cost budget for the org is exceeded.
- As a compliance reviewer, I want fallback outputs to pass the same safety filter or to be replaced with a neutral canned message if safety cannot be guaranteed.

Acceptance criteria (rough)
- API supports a flag: allow_partial=true/false (default false). When true, server may emit one or more partial results and a final completion event.
- Model routing policy supports a prioritized list of fallback model ids per route (config-driven).
- Fallback routing is traceable in logs and Console with reason codes (latency_budget_exceeded, cost_budget_exceeded, model_error).
- Safety filter runs on all fallback outputs; if filter fails, system returns neutral fallback with safe_reason header.

API / SDK notes
- Introduce a new event type in streaming (event: partial, confidence: numeric, fallback_chain: [ids as string]) — we can encode fallback_chain as a comma-separated string in metadata to avoid nested JSON.
- Add route config: fallback_priority = "redwood/1q8-small,redwood/4q-distill,neutral:we-cant-answer"
- Expose route metrics: partial_rate, fallback_rate, fallback_latency_delta, safety-filter-blocks

Operational concerns
- Increased tracing cardinality — need to sample fallback events initially. Add a Console toggle to show all fallback traces.
- Cost accounting: when a request hits a fallback chain, charge the actual tokens used across models. For accounting simplicity, record the final model used and annotate with fallback_attempts="2".

Rollout plan (phased)
1) Internal dogfood: enable allow_partial=true for redwood-internal routes only. Monitor partial_rate and client patch rate.
2) Beta: opt-in per-customer route config, surface metrics in Console.
3) Gradual opt-in default for low-tier plans as an explicit cost-saving toggle.

Success metrics
- Decrease in hard failures due to latency/timeouts by 40% on dogfood routes.
- Average latency perceived by end-users reduces by 20% (more partial early content).
- Fallbacks that trigger safety blocked < 0.1% of fallback events.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to represent partial merges on client side? (we should file a small client SDK note; for now, event with sequence id + patch text)
- Safety: for distilled/quantized variants we can't guarantee parity — do we allow a lower safety threshold or always use filter? Likely always run filter for now.
- Billing: do we expose a capped token charge when partials are returned? Or charge normally? Need finance input (cc: @Owen).
- E2E test plan: create synthetic load tests that force fallback chains and validate correctness and billing.

Next steps (short list)
- Spike: implement server-side streaming partial event and simple fallback chain resolver (1 engineer, 3 days).
- Add metrics to runtime (prometheus-ish counters): fallback_attempts_total, partial_events_total, fallback_reasons_total (labels).
- Write a small Console widget to show fallback events per-route (design: simple list + sample traces).
- Sync with Safety (Liang) on filter requirements for cheap variants.

Notes to self
- Keep the UX primitives minimal: event type + confidence + final marker. Avoid changing existing streaming wire format too much.
- This pairs well with session-priority work (eviction/restore) but is orthogonal; can reuse session budget concepts.

Random sketches (brainstorm)
- "Progressive fidelity" — partial responses could be marked as TL;DRs that expand when final arrives.
- "Client hint header" — clients can provide display_budget=inline|defer so server knows if partials are helpful.
- "Safe neutral templates" per language/region for when safety filter blocks cheap fallback.

End of pad.
